risks: only 3 validation windows: weight estimation is high variance
diagnosis.narrative: The series is dominated by a moderate downward trend (a net fall of ~66% of its level). Seasonality is strong (period 48): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The series is quite predictable: its energy concentrates in a few structured frequencies. The series reads as ambiguous by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (1515 points, ~4% of the sample). The series crosses zero, so percentage errors are unstable and mean-based combinations are safer than ratio-based ones. Across validation windows the model ranking is moderate (Kendall tau 0.473), which favours a weighted combination.

Seasonal dominance and moderate ranking stability suggest a robust trimmed‑mean may reduce influence of outlier models while keeping most of the pool.

The series is strongly seasonal and has moderate ranking stability; a weighted combination is suggested by the hint, but the current inverse_error weights performed poorly. A softmax-based weighting may smooth extreme weights and better handle the high variance in only 3 windows.
Use a metric-ranked subset (trend moderate, seasonal strong) to reduce noise from weak models and try weighted inverse_error on that subset.
test a per‑horizon weighted scheme (best_per_horizon) on the full pool to capture horizon‑specific strengths.
The series is seasonal dominated with moderate ranking stability; a simple mean over the full pool may capture complementary strengths without overfitting to few windows.
Try a per‑horizon weighted scheme on the reduced pool4 to capture horizon‑specific strengths while staying within the weighted hint.
Test a weighted combination on the smaller, stable pool4 using softmax_neg_error weights to exploit complementary strengths while reducing variance from many models.
Use a forward selection weight to capture complementary models across horizons, which may improve over simple weighted schemes given moderate ranking stability and multiple correlated groups.
test a per‑horizon weighted scheme using the top‑k‐per‑horizon handle w10 on the full pool to capture horizon‑specific strengths.
